Attacks against civilians by Arab militia fighters and RSF in a mosque in the al-Jamarek neighborhood and the government's Labor Office, an IDP gathering site, led to the deaths of 46 people with 8 injured. Explosive munitions fell in al-Jabal, al-Nasseem, al-Shati, and Um Duwein, killing 12 civilians. Two Masalit women were raped by Arab militia fighters, and one woman was beaten while they were looking for her husband who is a well-known community leader. The clash led to the displacement of thousands of citizens from the south and east of the city to the north as well as the loss of electricity and water in the city. At least one home and a shop were looted by the RSF, injuring 1 person. Specific fatalities for this event: 58 (46 IDPs + 12 from shelling). Based on a May 2024 HRW report, 1835 fatalities were added to events between 20 April and 15 July in El Geneina. 723 of these fatalities could not be attributed to specific events and were split between 34 armed clashes and attacks in the period 24 April to 15 June during the height of hostilities in the city. 21 coded to this event. Total fatalities coded as 79 (46 + 12 + 21).

Clashes took place in al-Buhaira, al-Ghabat, al-Jabal, al-Jamarek, al-Madaress, al-Majliss, al-Mansoura, al-Tadhamun, al-Thawra, and al-Zuhur. RSF and their allies attacked the Gilani and al-Hashab IDP camps in al-Ghabat. One witness counted 80 injured people and 27 dead from the attacks on the camps. Gunmen in civilian clothes in RSF vehicles attacked al-Atig mosque in al-Thawra. Damage from the attack also caused the ship to lose all propulsion and ultimately sink on 9 July. Other ships owned by the owner of the Eternity C had recently called in Israel. The Russian sailor was released around 2 April 2026.
